name: Abū al-Saʿādāt Hibat Allāh ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥamza al-ʿAlawī
summary: Baghdad grammarian of the Saljūq age, head of the descendants of ʿAlī in al-Karkh, whose Amālī record eighty-four sessions of grammar; the teacher of Ibn al-Anbārī.
bio: Ibn al-Shajarī was a descendant of ʿAlī and served as their headman (naqīb) in al-Karkh in Baghdad. He taught grammar for some seventy years, and his al-Amālī al-Shajariyya, dictated in eighty-four sessions, treats questions of grammar, the Qurʾān and poetry, with frequent disagreement with earlier masters. He also made an anthology of poetry, al-Ḥamāsa. Abū al-Barakāt ibn al-Anbārī was his student. He died in 542/1148.
